task: Distinguish simulated proton-proton collision events in which a Higgs boson is produced (signal) from background events.
instructions: You are helping a feature-selection search for a classification task. Rate how useful each feature is likely to be for predicting the class, on its own or together with a few others, from 0 (useless) to 1 (most useful). Use only your knowledge of the domain and the descriptions given; you do not see the data. Reply with a JSON object only: {"scores": {"<feature index>": <score>, ...}} with one entry for every feature index listed.

calls.reply:
This looks like the HIGGS dataset (UCI). I'm assuming the standard column order, since the feature names are not informative.

Assumed order:
- 0: lepton pT
- 1: lepton eta
- 2: lepton phi
- 3: missing energy magnitude
- 4: missing energy phi
- 5-8: jet 1 (pT, eta, phi, b-tag)
- 9-12: jet 2 (pT, eta, phi, b-tag)
- 13-16: jet 3 (pT, eta, phi, b-tag)
- 17-20: jet 4 (pT, eta, phi, b-tag)
- 21: m_jj
- 22: m_jjj
- 23: m_lv
- 24: m_jlv
- 25: m_bb
- 26: m_wbb
- 27: m_wwbb

The high-level masses are the most useful, and m_bb (25), m_wbb (26) and m_wwbb (27) are the strongest of them. Among the low-level features, lepton pT (0), missing energy (3) and the jet pTs are moderately informative. Eta and phi features carry almost no signal on their own, and the b-tags carry some.
